accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 1.G.3 (partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe them with halves, fourths and quarters, understand that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares) and the DfE Year 1 fractions statutory text (a half as one of two equal parts, a quarter as one of four equal parts) with the NCETM Year 1 spine notes. Every share in the lab is drawn with exact equal angles or widths; the folding count (1, 2, 4, 8 parts) is 2 to the power of the folds; two quarters exactly fill a half because the quarter pieces are half the width and half the height. m9 and the adult text add the same-whole condition, which the standard assumes.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the whole-number bias documented in NCETM fractions guidance and in Behr, Lesh, Post and Silver's rational-number research (a quarter is bigger because 4 is more than 2: prediction 3 first option, 'count' feedback, p1, m2), the belief that any four parts are quarters (Fair shares step with unequal strips and an off-centre cut, 'unequal' feedback, p5, m3), the idea that the share stays the same when more people share ('same'), the fold slip of 3 parts after 2 folds (prediction 2, 'fold'), and comparing parts of different wholes (m9).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmoresh is built around one mechanism, one whole cut into more equal shares: a pizza that re-cuts as friends are seated with the one-share slice and a dashed ghost of the 2-share slice side by side, a sheet that doubles its parts per fold with a shrinking size bar, draggable quarter tiles that snap onto a half, a five-shape equal-or-not judge, and five same-size-pizza slices ordered by number of sharers. flagfcmp (ages 7-8) cuts a bar and orders written unit fractions with < and >; this lab has no fraction notation. Gate lab_distinct passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the slice shrink before the text names quarters; the fold bars visibly halve each time; a single quarter leaves a gap on the half and the second one closes it, which is the moment the quarter-is-smaller idea lands; wrong judgements in Fair shares say what to check (are the parts the same size); the slice line can only be built biggest first, and a wrong tap names the slice shared by fewer people as bigger.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'bigger' or 'the same size' when 4 share instead of 2 (the one-share slice shrinks inside the ghost half), '3' parts after two folds (the sheet shows 4), 'a quarter, because 4 is more than 2' (one quarter does not cover the half), and 'shared by 8' as the biggest slice (it is the smallest in the line).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions rotating answer order, with six distinct feedback messages naming the slip: more pieces is not bigger pieces; the whole is unchanged but cut into more parts; quarters must be equal; each fold doubles the parts; a quarter is half of a half so two cover a half; sharing with more people never enlarges a slice.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 0.2 with sentences of 5 to 12 words built on pizza, half, quarter, fold; adult text averages 5.8 with one denser paragraph for the common mistakes, under the 9.5 limit overall. Lab step text is one or two short sentences; canvas labels are single words (whole, half, quarter, eighth) or short phrases; slices are labelled with plain numbers and a key line.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (halves, quarters, more sharers means smaller with fair shares, folding). Items vary: p2 cuts halves into k pieces, p4 counts quarters on h halves, m5 asks what to do when two more people arrive, m8 counts slices left, m9 checks the same-whole rule.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for the start state and after Show me on every step: pizza, ghost slice and headline pill fit at 390 px; fold bars and their labels do not overlap; the two squares and dragged quarters stay inside the canvas; the five judged shapes are shown as labelled thumbnails at the end; the slice line uses number tags after the long 'shared by' labels overlapped in the first pass. Young-layout buttons wrap to two rows without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Add a friend and Take one away, Fold and Unfold, Lay a quarter on the half, Equal shares and Not equal, and one Shared by n button per slice. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each result (number of slices, parts after folding, how much of the half is covered, why a cut is or is not equal). Challenge feedback is a polite live region; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
